paragraphs.text: OpenAI has updated the dictation feature in ChatGPT so that spoken words turn into text while the user is still speaking, rather than after the recording ends. The company calls the update Live Dictation and announced it on November 18, 2026, according to 9to5Mac and iThinkDifferent. The same update removes the 10 minute recording limit that previously cut dictation off.

In a post on X, the official ChatGPT account said dictation was getting faster and more reliable, 9to5Mac reported. Atty Eleti, who works on voice at OpenAI, also confirmed on X that the 10 minute cap had been lifted.

Until this update, the transcript only appeared once the user stopped talking, so long recordings meant a wait before the text showed up. iThinkDifferent reported that OpenAI says the live approach cuts that wait.

According to OpenAI's release notes, as quoted by 9to5Mac, the running transcript is optional: users can tap or click the waveform to show or hide the text while they talk. Superpower Daily noted that dictation still starts from the microphone icon in the message box.

The release notes say Live Dictation is rolling out globally to all ChatGPT plans on iOS, Android, the web and the desktop app, 9to5Mac reported. That includes free accounts. iThinkDifferent added that the feature may take some time to reach every account, so not all users will see it at once.

OpenAI has not announced a new maximum recording length to replace the old 10 minute cap, Superpower Daily pointed out, so it is not confirmed that recordings are unlimited. The company also did not publish figures on how much faster or more accurate the new transcription is.
Settings for sharing audio and for allowing conversations to improve OpenAI's models are separate from dictation and sit in ChatGPT's data controls, according to Superpower Daily.
Part of a wider voice overhaul

The change follows several other voice updates in ChatGPT this year. In August, OpenAI changed the Android app so the dictation button stays available after text or attachments are added to a message, iThinkDifferent reported. ChatGPT Voice, built on GPT-Live, launched on July 8, and the older Advanced and Standard voice options are set to be retired from ChatGPT Voice on December 11, 2026.

OpenAI is also retiring the ChatGPT Classic app for Mac on January 30, 2027, according to iThinkDifferent. The newer desktop app shows the same conversations, and it is one of the platforms receiving Live Dictation.

Removing the 10 minute cap matters most for people who use dictation to draft long material, such as notes after a meeting, a rough essay or a detailed prompt. Seeing the words appear in real time also makes it easier to catch a misheard name before the message is sent. With no stated replacement limit, heavy users will likely find the practical ceiling through use rather than documentation.

Watch whether OpenAI publishes a new maximum recording length or accuracy figures as Live Dictation reaches all accounts, and how the December 11 voice changes affect people who rely on ChatGPT by voice.
